stages.title: ENDOGENIC PROCESSES AND THE PLATE-TECTONIC FRAME
stages.terms: Endogenic geomorphic activity includes tectonism, orogeny, epeirogeny, earthquakes and vulcanism generated by mantle heat, gravity, isostatic adjustment and lithospheric-plate interaction.
stages.mechanism: plate motion concentrates compression, tension, shear and melting
stages.consequence: convergent belts host arcs + deep quakes; transforms host quakes without major volcanism
stages.trap: plate setting is the regional driver, not a substitute for rupture/magma mechanics
stages.answer: Earthquakes and vulcanism are surface expressions of an internally powered, mobile lithosphere: plate motion supplies the regional setting, while fault rupture or magma ascent supplies the immediate mechanism.

stages.title: STRESS, STRAIN, ELASTIC REBOUND AND FAULTS
stages.terms: An earthquake commonly results from brittle failure and coseismic slip on a fault after tectonic stress produces elastic strain; elastic rebound is the partial recovery of deformed rock blocks after rupture.
stages.mechanism: load - lock - strain accumulation - rupture/slip - elastic rebound
stages.trap: a mapped fault indicates a source possibility, not the time of the next earthquake
stages.answer: The earthquake is sudden, but its preparation is usually slow: stress loads a locked fault, elastic strain accumulates, rupture begins when resistance is exceeded, and released energy radiates as seismic waves.

stages.title: EARTHQUAKE TERMINOLOGY, CAUSES AND CLASSIFICATIONS
stages.terms: An earthquake is the transient vibration of the ground caused by seismic-wave radiation from a sudden source, most commonly fault rupture but also volcanic, collapse, reservoir-associated, induced or explosion sources.
stages.mechanism: source class + focal depth + tectonic setting explain where and how shaking begins
stages.consequence: shallow often damages locally; deep slab events may be widely felt but differently expressed
stages.trap: depth influences shaking, but vulnerability determines whether hazard becomes disaster
stages.answer: Earthquake classification must distinguish the source mechanism, focal depth and tectonic setting; “tectonic earthquake” is the dominant class, not the only possible source of ground vibration.

stages.title: FOCUS, EPICENTRE, SEISMOGRAPHS AND LOCATING AN EVENT
stages.terms: The hypocentre/focus is the calculated subsurface origin of seismic radiation, while the epicentre is its vertical surface projection; a seismometer senses motion and a seismograph/seismic station records a time series called a seismogram.
stages.mechanism: one station gives distance - three or more station circles intersect - epicentre is estimated
stages.consequence: epicentre locates the surface projection; worst damage may occur elsewhere
stages.trap: a single station cannot supply both distance and unique direction
stages.answer: Focus and epicentre identify source geometry, not damage ranking: the worst-hit locality may lie away from the epicentre because rupture directivity, basin amplification and vulnerable construction modify shaking.

stages.title: P, S, LOVE AND RAYLEIGH WAVES
stages.terms: Body waves comprise compressional P waves and shear S waves travelling through the Earth; surface waves comprise Love and Rayleigh modes guided near the surface and commonly producing large damaging motions.
stages.mechanism: elastic properties control velocity, particle motion and permitted medium
stages.consequence: P arrives first and crosses liquids; S is stopped by liquid; surface waves strongly affect structures
stages.trap: transverse S motion is not the same as horizontal-only Love motion
stages.answer: P and S waves diagnose the Earth's interior because their velocity and permitted media differ, whereas Love and Rayleigh waves dominate the near-surface damage problem because their amplitudes and durations can be large.

stages.title: REFRACTION, DISCONTINUITIES AND SHADOW ZONES
stages.terms: Seismic shadow zones are angular regions where direct wave phases are absent because P waves are strongly refracted at the core–mantle boundary and S waves cannot propagate through the liquid outer core.
stages.mechanism: P bends strongly through the core; S cannot cross a liquid outer core
stages.consequence: P later reappears; direct S remains absent on the far side
stages.trap: S-wave absence proves liquid outer core, not an entirely liquid core
stages.answer: The Earth’s deep interior is known by wave behaviour rather than direct observation: P-wave refraction and S-wave extinction reveal sharp discontinuities and the liquid state of the outer core.

stages.title: MAGNITUDE, INTENSITY AND LOGARITHMIC ENERGY
stages.terms: Magnitude is an instrument-derived event parameter—large events are commonly reported using moment magnitude Mw—whereas intensity scales such as MMI or MSK classify observed shaking and effects at individual locations.
stages.mechanism: seismic moment estimates source size; observations classify place-specific shaking
stages.consequence: one magnitude but multiple intensities and unequal losses
stages.trap: never convert a magnitude directly into a fixed damage category
stages.answer: An earthquake has one estimated magnitude but many intensities, because rupture size is an event property while local effects vary with distance, depth, path, ground and buildings.

stages.title: GLOBAL EARTHQUAKE DISTRIBUTION AND PLATE MARGINS
stages.terms: Earthquake distribution maps delineate subduction Wadati–Benioff zones, mid-ocean ridges, transform faults, continental collision belts and a smaller population of intraplate sources.
stages.mechanism: subduction gives shallow-deep seismicity; ridges/transforms give shallow seismicity; inherited faults reactivate inside plates
stages.consequence: seismic belts overlap volcano belts strongly but not perfectly
stages.trap: collision Himalaya is seismic without being a typical oceanic-subduction volcanic arc
stages.answer: The global map of seismicity is a map of plate interaction: shallow events outline almost every boundary, while inclined shallow-to-deep zones uniquely reveal subducting slabs.

stages.title: SECONDARY HAZARDS, SITE RESPONSE AND THE RISK EQUATION
stages.terms: Earthquake risk is the potential loss arising from seismic hazard interacting with exposure, physical/social vulnerability and coping capacity; cascading hazards include liquefaction, slope failure, fire, surface rupture, dam failure and tsunami.
stages.mechanism: source - path - site - building/network response - cascade
stages.consequence: equal magnitude does not produce equal loss across sites or societies
stages.trap: do not use earthquake, hazard, risk and disaster as synonyms
stages.answer: An earthquake is a hazard event; it becomes a disaster when shaking and cascades strike exposed, vulnerable systems whose coping capacity is exceeded.

stages.title: TSUNAMI GENERATION, PROPAGATION AND COASTAL IMPACT
stages.terms: Tsunamis are long-period gravity waves most commonly produced by rapid vertical sea-floor displacement during submarine megathrust earthquakes, but also by volcanic collapse/eruption, submarine landslides or rare impacts.
stages.mechanism: submarine rupture - deep-ocean propagation - shallow-water amplification - coastal flooding
stages.consequence: low wave offshore can become destructive onshore; first wave need not be largest
stages.trap: tsunami is a seismic/gravity wave train, not a tidal wave
stages.answer: A tsunami is not a wind wave or tide: it begins with sudden water-column displacement, crosses deep ocean with low height and high speed, and grows destructively as shoaling compresses the wave near the coast.

stages.title: VOLCANO ANATOMY, MAGMA, LAVA, SILICA, GAS AND VISCOSITY
stages.terms: Vulcanism comprises magma generation, ascent, intrusion and extrusion; magma is molten or partially molten subsurface material containing crystals and volatiles, while lava is magma erupted at the surface.
stages.mechanism: silica + lower temperature + crystals - viscosity - trapped gas - fragmentation
stages.consequence: basaltic magma tends effusive; silicic magma tends explosive
stages.trap: volcano shape is an outcome; magma rheology is the mechanism
stages.answer: Eruption style is controlled less by the size of a cone than by magma rheology: silica-rich, cooler and gas-charged magma is commonly more viscous and explosive, whereas hotter basaltic magma generally allows easier degassing and effusive flow.

stages.title: INTRUSIVE AND EXTRUSIVE FORMS; VOLCANIC PRODUCTS
stages.terms: Intrusive igneous bodies crystallise below the surface in concordant or discordant forms, whereas extrusive vulcanism constructs lava plains, cones, domes and pyroclastic deposits from erupted products.
stages.mechanism: emplacement geometry forms intrusions; fragmentation and flow form extrusive products
stages.consequence: dyke cuts layers, sill follows layers; pyroclastic current is hot gas-debris, lahar is water-debris
stages.trap: ash, sulphur compounds and nitrogen species are eruption products, not only lava
stages.answer: Intrusive forms record the geometry of magma emplacement, while extrusive forms record the interaction of lava viscosity, gas, eruption rate, relief and erosion at the surface.

stages.title: ERUPTION STYLES, VOLCANO TYPES AND ACTIVITY STATUS
stages.terms: Eruption-style classifications arrange behaviour from sustained effusive fissure or fountain activity to intermittent explosions and high-column Plinian/Pelean activity; morphology includes shield, composite, cinder, dome and caldera systems.
stages.mechanism: easy degassing - effusion; trapped gas + viscous magma - fragmentation/explosion
stages.consequence: style, landform and activity status are independent classification axes
stages.trap: absence of a recent historical eruption does not by itself prove extinction
stages.answer: Eruption style, volcano shape and activity status are three separate classifications: fluid lava can build a shield, alternating lava and tephra can build a stratovolcano, and neither shape alone determines whether a volcano is extinct.

stages.title: PLATE-SETTING VOLCANISM, RING OF FIRE AND MID-OCEAN RIDGES
stages.terms: Boundary volcanism results from decompression melting at divergent margins and flux melting above subduction slabs, producing contrasting basaltic ridge/rift systems and commonly explosive volcanic arcs.
stages.mechanism: divergence lowers pressure; subduction adds volatiles to the mantle wedge
stages.consequence: ridges yield basaltic crust; arcs yield mixed, often explosive stratovolcanism
stages.trap: Ring of Fire means a geophysical system, not a perfect geometric circle
stages.answer: Divergent volcanism is generated mainly by pressure release in upwelling mantle, whereas subduction volcanism is promoted by slab-derived volatiles that lower the melting temperature of the mantle wedge.

stages.title: MANTLE PLUMES, HOT SPOTS AND FLOOD BASALTS
stages.terms: In the plume hypothesis, a buoyant thermal anomaly rises through the mantle; a broad plume head may produce a large igneous province, while a narrower persistent tail forms a hot spot and an age-progressive volcanic chain as the plate moves overhead.
stages.mechanism: head reaches lithosphere - voluminous fissure basalt; moving plate over tail - volcanic chain
stages.consequence: Deccan plateau differs from an arc cone; hot-spot trail records plate motion
stages.trap: plume hypothesis is a standard but qualified explanation, not a settled universal cause
stages.answer: Mantle plumes complement plate-boundary theory by explaining selected intraplate volcanic chains and flood-basalt provinces, while hot-spot age progression provides an independent record of plate motion.

stages.title: CONSTRUCTIVE, DESTRUCTIVE, CLIMATIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS
stages.terms: Volcanic impacts operate through lava, tephra, density currents, lahars, gases and aerosols at event scales, and through crustal construction, nutrient release, hydrothermal mineralisation and atmospheric forcing at longer scales.
stages.mechanism: product + height + wind + relief + water control the impact footprint
stages.consequence: short-term destruction/cooling can coexist with long-term land, soil and resource benefits
stages.trap: ash is not the principal long-lived global cooling agent; stratospheric sulphate aerosol is
stages.answer: Volcanism is geographically double-edged: episodic high-intensity hazards coexist with persistent benefits such as fertile weathered material, geothermal energy, mineralisation and new crust.

stages.title: INDIA'S TECTONIC FRAMEWORK AND REGIONAL SEISMIC RISK
stages.terms: India's seismicity reflects Indian–Eurasian convergence, Indo-Burmese deformation, Sunda–Andaman subduction and reactivation of inherited intraplate structures within the Peninsular shield.
stages.mechanism: collision/subduction drive boundary seismicity; old faults can reactivate inside the plate
stages.consequence: Himalaya/Andaman are boundary systems; Kachchh/Latur/Koyna correct the “stable means aseismic” error
stages.trap: Indo-Gangetic alluvium may amplify Himalayan shaking far from the mountain source
stages.answer: India does not possess one earthquake belt but a mosaic of collision, subduction, syntaxis, rift-reactivation and intraplate settings, each requiring a different source explanation and risk lens.

stages.title: INDIA SEISMIC ZONATION, MICROZONATION AND CLASSIFICATION CAUTION
stages.terms: Macrozonation assigns broad design-hazard classes using national-scale seismic evidence, while microzonation integrates geology, seismotectonics, ground motion, soil and site response to produce finer GIS-based hazard or risk products.
stages.mechanism: national evidence defines broad design zones; local geology/soil/groundwater refine site response
stages.consequence: zone map guides design but neither macro- nor microzonation predicts event time
stages.trap: disclose the 2025/2026 official inconsistency instead of asserting an unverified settled Zone VI code
stages.answer: Zonation is a design and planning input, not an earthquake prediction: macrozones generalise regional hazard, while microzonation resolves the local soil, basin and liquefaction contrasts that determine neighbourhood-level shaking.

stages.title: INSTITUTIONS, RESILIENT CONSTRUCTION, EARLY WARNING LIMITS AND PREPAREDNESS
stages.terms: Seismic risk reduction combines monitoring, hazard assessment, code-compliant ductile design, non-structural safety, retrofitting, land-use control, lifeline continuity, drills, public education and rapid warning/response systems.
stages.mechanism: monitor/map - design/enforce - retrofit lifelines - secure non-structural elements - drill/communicate
stages.consequence: early warning may provide seconds after rupture; prediction claims event before rupture
stages.trap: codes on paper do not reduce vulnerability without local adoption, supervision and compliance
stages.answer: Since deterministic earthquake prediction is unavailable, public policy must shift from forecasting the event to reducing the consequences through safer sites, ductile structures, retrofitted lifelines and practised community action.
